# aberrations.py
*`src/pySEA/rayTEM/aberrations.py`*

Axial wave aberrations in Krivanek notation, and how to apply them.

---

## Module-level functions

### `krivanek_terms(max_order)` *(line 17)*
The Krivanek ``C_{n,m}`` term names up to a given order.

Generated, not tabulated: `for n in 1..max: for m in range(n+1, -1, -2)`. That
loop *is* the naming rule — order `n` carries multiplicities `n+1, n-1, ...`
down to 0 or 1 — so extending to higher order is a parameter change, not a new
table to get wrong.

`KRIVANEK_TERMS = krivanek_terms(5)` is the module-level table everything else
consults; 14 terms.

Cross-repo: the stems match `sea_eco.io`'s `abb_C` list exactly (its swift
reader is the source of measured coefficients). If you extend one, extend the
other — there is a test that compares them.

## Aberrations *(class · line 89)*
A set of axial aberration coefficients, and the phase they produce.

| Method | Kind | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `Aberrations.__init__(self, coefficients, convention)` | method | Create a coefficient set. |
| `Aberrations.order_and_multiplicity(name)` | staticmethod | Look up ``(n, m)`` for a term name. |
| `Aberrations.items(self)` | method | Iterate ``(name, complex)`` over the nonzero terms. |
| `Aberrations.setdefault(self, name, value)` | method | Set a coefficient only if it is not already nonzero. |
| `Aberrations.as_dict(self)` | method | The nonzero coefficients as ``{name: complex}``. |
| `Aberrations.from_letters(cls, coefficients)` | classmethod | Build from the letter notation (``C1``, ``A1``, ``B2``, ``S3``...). |
| `Aberrations.to_letters(self)` | method | Express the stored set in the letter notation. |
| `Aberrations.from_metadata(cls, metadata)` | classmethod | Read coefficients as sea-eco's swift reader stores them. |
| `Aberrations.phase_at(self, X, Y, wavelength, power)` | method | The wave aberration function :math:`\chi` at given coordinates. |
| `Aberrations.deflection_at(self, X, Y, power)` | method | The transverse ray aberration at given coordinates, for every term. |
| `Aberrations.phase(self, shape, dx, dy, wavelength, power)` | method | The wave aberration function :math:`\chi` on a sampled grid. |
| `Aberrations.gradient(self, shape, dx, dy, wavelength, power)` | method | ``(∂χ/∂x, ∂χ/∂y)`` on a sampled grid, in radians per metre. |

**Why a class.** Aberrations used to live as 25 flat scalars on `Lens` plus a
letter-named table in `waveoptics`, so the ray path implemented `C3` alone
while the wave path implemented everything, and adding a term meant editing
three places. One object holds the coefficients and answers both questions.

**Storage.** Parallel `names`/`real`/`imag` lists, not a dict and not a complex
array — `.sea` carries scalars, strings, bools and sequences. The class is
itself a `SEASerializable`, so it nests: an element writes it as a child node.
`convention` records which notation the names are in, so a bare set of numbers
is never ambiguous.

**Complex coefficients.** `C_{n,m} = a + ib` fixes size *and* orientation,
matching a Nion file's `.a`/`.b` pair. `a` is aligned with x, `b` at 45°/m;
equivalently `|c|cos(m(φ − arg(c)/m))`. `m = 0` terms are rotationally
symmetric and reject a nonzero `b` rather than ignoring it.

**One function, two representations.** The wave multiplies by `exp(iχ)` from
`phase_at`; rays take `(1/k)∇χ` from `deflection_at`. Same χ, so they cannot
disagree — see `elements.Element.aberration_kick`, which only decides *where
along the element* the kick acts, and `elements.Lens.phase_shift`.

Related: `elements.Element.aberrations` (where one is attached),
`elements.Lens.aberration_powers` (which terms the scaled frame absorbs),
`elements.suspended_aberrations` (how `apply_aberrations=False` works).

### `Aberrations.setdefault(self, name, value)` *(line 351)*
Set a coefficient only if it is not already nonzero.

Used where a default must not overwrite a term the caller named explicitly.
(It was introduced for `Lens(Cs=)`, which has since been removed — `C30` is
spherical aberration, and one alias for one term is exactly the
per-aberration specificity this module exists to remove.)

### `Aberrations.from_letters(cls, coefficients)` *(line 405)*
Build from the letter notation (``C1``, ``A1``, ``B2``, ``S3``...).

The letter format (`C1`/`A1`/`B2`/`S3`/`D4`...) is a **different notation for
the same quantities**, common in corrector software — not a different set of
aberrations. Converted on the way in via `LETTER_TO_KRIVANEK` so there is only
ever one stored convention.

### `Aberrations.from_metadata(cls, metadata)` *(line 460)*
Read coefficients as sea-eco's swift reader stores them.

Performs the `a`/`b` → complex step that `sea_eco.io`'s swift reader
deliberately leaves undone — the reader stores the components as the file gives
them, because combining them needs to know the target convention.

Searches by **leaf name**, not by path (`_flatten_metadata`), because
instrument metadata nests aberrations differently per detector
(`Instrument/Condensers/Aberrations` vs `Instrument/Aberrations`). Either the
whole metadata tree or just the sub-tree can be passed.

Unknown keys are ignored rather than raising: instrument metadata legitimately
carries entries this class does not model.

### `Aberrations.phase_at(self, X, Y, wavelength, power)` *(line 574)*
The wave aberration function :math:`\chi` at given coordinates.

Takes **coordinates**, not a grid, so the same code serves a wavefield and a
ray table. `phase()` is the grid wrapper.

Sign convention is this package's: a converging lens carries `χ = −k r²/2f` and
the field is multiplied by `exp(iχ)` — the opposite sign to texts writing
`exp(−iχ)`. With it, positive `C30` focuses marginal rays short.

Written on the **element plane**, where ray height is proportional to pupil
angle (`θ = r·P`). That is why a nonzero focal power is required: with no
power there is no pupil angle to measure θ against.

### `Aberrations.deflection_at(self, X, Y, power)` *(line 627)*
The transverse ray aberration at given coordinates, for every term.

**Takes no wavelength**, and that is not an oversight: χ ∝ k, so `(1/k)∇χ` is
wavelength-free. Ray tables may carry no wavelength at all (`Source(voltage=None)`
leaves `E = 0`), and this still works.

Exact in the eikonal limit at **every** order, which is what makes the ray path
generic — one expression covers `C10` through `C56`.

Analytic, not a finite difference. Regular on axis: every term carries `θⁿ`
with `n ≥ 1`. Verified against a central difference of `phase_at` to ~2e-11
relative across seven terms of five different orders.

Worth knowing: for `C10` (n=1, m=0) this reduces to `−C10·P²·x`, a pure power
change, so a traced parallel bundle crosses at `1/(P + C10 P²)` — the same
plane the scaled frame reports. That is why `C10` must **not** also fold into
`focal_power`; it would be applied twice.

### `Aberrations.gradient(self, shape, dx, dy, wavelength, power)` *(line 740)*
``(∂χ/∂x, ∂χ/∂y)`` on a sampled grid, in radians per metre.

`k` times `deflection_at`, on a grid. Provided for code that wants the phase
slope itself; **ray propagation should use `deflection_at`**, which needs no
wavelength.
